time.desc: For the first time, the country's trade chief and senior national security officials shared the stage to issue a tough warning to major trade rivals on rare earth export restrictions, and revealed that they are drafting higher tariffs and key technology export restrictions as countermeasures.
The country’s president signed an executive order to impose new tariffs on imported medium and heavy-duty trucks and set exemption rules for compliant products under regional trade agreements.
The country’s president announced the suspension of all trade negotiations with neighboring countries, citing a political ad involving a tariff dispute.

The country’s trade chief announced that he and his major trading partners have reached a framework for economic and trade arrangements and paved the way for a leaders’ meeting. The framework covers expanded agricultural product procurement and cooperation in the control of toxic chemicals.
The upper house of the country’s legislative body passed a resolution seeking to terminate the president’s emergency authorization to impose tariffs on neighboring countries.
The country's top judicial body held a hearing on the legality of the president's emergency authorization to impose widespread tariffs and raised multiple questions about the government's basis.
The country’s president signed an order to grant tariff exemptions to many types of food and agricultural products that are difficult to supply domestically to ease price pressures.
The country’s president threatens additional tariffs on goods from neighboring countries and sets cutoffs, citing cross-border water disputes

The president of the country announced that he would impose new punitive tariffs on third countries that trade with sanctioned countries, but did not simultaneously release a complete official implementation document.

The president of the country threatened that if neighboring countries continue to advance economic and trade arrangements with major trade rivals, they will impose extremely high tariffs on their imported goods and declared that they will take effect immediately.

After the country's highest judicial body ruled that the president's emergency authorization to impose tariffs on many countries exceeded his authority, the president quickly changed to another temporary authorization route to announce the imposition of new unified tariffs on global imported goods and an increase in tax rates.

The country’s trade representative announced the launch of new trade investigations on issues such as “overcapacity” against a number of major trading partners to find alternative legal basis for subsequent increases in tariffs.

The president of the country signed an executive order to impose extremely high tariffs on imported patented brand drugs, and required local production or participation in pricing arrangements as conditions for exemptions and exemptions, while also setting up buffer periods and exemptions.

The country’s government adjusted the national security metal tariff system and simplified the taxation rules for derivatives, reducing or exempting some low-metal content goods and specific equipment from tariffs.

The president of the country threatened to impose high tariffs on the basis of reports that his opponents may supply weapons to countries in war zones, further tying trade penalties to security issues.

After the emergency authorization of tariffs was found to be illegal, the country's customs launched preparations for a large-scale tariff refund system and opened importer registration to process tax refunds

Vehicles that meet the Agreement A trade terms are partially exempted, and only their non-domestic parts are taxed. Auto parts that meet the Agreement B standard are temporarily not affected by new truck tariffs; buses and long-distance buses are levied a 10% tariff.

Country Y The Trucking Associations have spoken out against new tariffs on medium- and heavy-duty trucks, noting they could further drive up prices at a time when the industry is already under pressure from steel tariffs.

Region P Governor M responded by announcing that the province was suspending advertising in Country Y starting a few days later to allow trade talks to resume, but that the ads would continue to air during the weekend's two events; Company K said the move had achieved the goal of delivering the message to the highest-level audiences.

The core contents of the framework agreement between Country Y and Country X include Country X significantly increasing the purchase of Country Y agricultural products, and Country X assisting in controlling the inflow of precursor chemicals used to make fentanyl Country Y; the two parties have reached a final agreement on the Product D transaction, and the details have been finalized and will be formally confirmed by the leaders of the two countries

Country Y Institution I2 Official A said that Leader A’s previous threat to impose 100% tariffs on Country X created a key bargaining chip for negotiations, and said that soybean farmers who have suffered losses from the trade war after the announcement of the agreement will be satisfied with the prospects for multiple quarters this and tomorrow.

Leader A disclosed on the special plane that his government was considering lowering Law Q in exchange for Country X making a commitment to curb the export of fentanyl precursor chemicals, explicitly linking trade policy with anti-drug issues for the first time; the ruling team A had previously imposed a 20% tariff on Country X imported goods on the grounds of fentanyl precursor control.

Country Y Institution V1 announces a hearing on the legality of Governance Team A’s global tariffs, Institution I2 Official A will attend the defense, Institution V1 hears the case with a 6-3 conservative majority; a lower court previously ruled that Leader A cited Law I to impose widespread tariffs beyond the authority of the president

Company F2 CEO Person Y2 said that the company has moved its supply chain from Country X to Country Q and other countries, but the tariffs in the new target countries are equally high or even higher, and the company can only struggle to avoid short-term bankruptcy

Region I Small business Company G2 co-founder Person Z2 became a direct victim of the trade war. She imported umbrellas and raincoats made of waterproof fabric from Country X. Law Q soared from 10% to 20% and then fell back to 145%. She was forced to cut expenses and lay off two operations and customer service staff.

At the tariff legality hearing, the majority of the justices raised sharp questions about Agency A's tariff policy. Leader A The appointed justice Person A3 questioned why so many countries need to apply reciprocal tariffs and pointed out that if the government loses the case, the refund process may become a mess; Institution I2 Nearly US$90 billion in import taxes have been collected so far. If the tariffs are found to be unconstitutional, refunds will be difficult.

Leader A once again issued a document reiterating the tariff threat to Country W, requiring it to deliver at least 200,000 acre feet of water to Region B2 before the cutoff, otherwise an additional 5% tariff will be imposed on Country W goods not covered by Agreement A, raising the tax rate to 30%; this request originated from the 1944 Law K obligation, Country W President J has not yet responded

Country X The Embassy in City C responded to Leader A’s 25% tariff threat to third countries, stating that Country X will take all necessary measures to safeguard its own interests, oppose any illegal unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction, and emphasized that there are no winners in tariff and trade wars.

The governments of Country G and Country I have stated that they are paying close attention to Leader A’s imposition of 25% tariffs on third countries trading with Country D; according to Institution Y1 data, more than 140 countries around the world still maintain trade relations with Country D, and Country X, as the largest buyer, purchased Country D77% of oil exports in 2024.
